title: Cisco Duo Bypass Code Generation
exclusions: Does not cover bypass status set on the user account itself; UC-10.7.21 covers that.
evidence: List of bypass codes issued with user, administrator, and matching ticket number.

controlTest.positiveScenario: In a test Duo account open a test user, choose Generate Bypass Codes, and save. After the next input interval the search returns one row with that user and the administrator.
controlTest.negativeScenario: Change the same test user's display name only. The administrator event is indexed with a different action, and the search returns no rows.

dataSources: `index=duo sourcetype=cisco:duo:administrator` from the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) Duo input, Administrator log type (`GET /admin/v1/logs/administrator`).
app: Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, [Splunkbase 7404](https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/7404)), Cisco Duo input. Replaces the deprecated Duo Splunk Connector (Splunkbase 3504, end of life 31 May 2026).
spl:
index=duo sourcetype="cisco:duo:administrator" action="bypass_create"
| rename object as user, username as admin
| stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(description) as description by action actionlabel user admin
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
description: Lists every Duo bypass code created by an administrator, with the user it was issued to, the administrator who issued it, and the code settings (uses and expiry) from the change description.
value: A bypass code is a password-equivalent second factor. Help-desk staff issue them for lost phones, which is exactly the pretext social engineers use; an unexpected code, or one with many uses or no expiry, is often the start of an account takeover.
implementation: Collect the Duo Administrator log with the Cisco Security Cloud (7404) Duo input into `index=duo`. Join the results to the help-desk ticket system on `user` and alert on codes with no matching ticket.
visualization: Alert table: firstTime, user, admin, description (uses and expiry). Supporting panel: bypass codes issued per administrator per week.

references.title: Cisco Security Cloud App for Splunk User Guide

knownFalsePositives:
1. **Lost or replaced phones** — the normal reason for a bypass code. Match `user` to an open help-desk ticket raised by that user before alerting.

2. **Self-service codes in test accounts** — exclude test users by name prefix.

**Suppression:** join to the ticketing system export on `user` and the same day.
detailedImplementation:
Prerequisites
• Cisco Security Cloud (`CiscoSecurityCloud`, Splunkbase 7404) on the search heads and on the heavy forwarder or Splunk Cloud Inputs Data Manager that runs its modular inputs. It replaces the Duo Splunk Connector (Splunkbase 3504, end of life 31 May 2026); disable the old connector's inputs after cutover so events are not indexed twice.
• A Duo Admin API application created by an Owner-role administrator in the Duo Admin Panel under Applications > Protect an Application > Admin API. Record the integration key, secret key, and API hostname (`api-XXXXXXXX.duosecurity.com`), and grant it **Grant read log**.
• Outbound HTTPS (TCP 443) from the input host to the API hostname, and an accurate system clock on that host, because the Admin API signs every request with the current date.
• An index for Duo data (this page uses `index=duo`) and a role with `srchIndexesAllowed` on it for the identity and SOC teams.

Step 1 — Configure data collection
• In Cisco Security Cloud open Application Setup, choose the Cisco Duo card, and create an input with the integration key, secret key, and API hostname. Enable the Administrator log type and set the index to `duo`.
• The input reads `GET /admin/v1/logs/administrator` and writes `sourcetype=cisco:duo:administrator`, one event per administrator action, with `action`, `actionlabel`, `description` (a JSON string of the changed settings), `object` (the policy, user, or integration acted on), and `username` (the administrator).
• Run `index=duo sourcetype=cisco:duo:administrator action=bypass_create | table _time username object description` to see the code settings Duo records.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert
```spl
index=duo sourcetype="cisco:duo:administrator" action="bypass_create"
| rename object as user, username as admin
| stats count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime values(description) as description by action actionlabel user admin
| convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
```

Understanding this SPL
• `action="bypass_create"` is the administrator log action Duo writes when codes are generated for a user.
• In this event `object` is the user the codes belong to and `username` is the administrator; both are renamed so the row reads clearly.
• `values(description)` keeps the code count, allowed uses, and expiry, which decide how risky each code is.

Step 3 — Validate
• Compare with the Duo admin console (Admin Panel) under Reports > Administrator Actions, filtered to bypass code actions.
• Open the user in Admin Panel > Users and confirm the bypass codes listed there match the alert.
• Run `index=duo sourcetype=cisco:duo:administrator | timechart span=1h count` over 7 days to confirm there are no collection gaps.

Step 4 — Operationalize
• Schedule every 15 minutes over the last 20 minutes. Alert only when no help-desk ticket exists for `user` that day.
• Weekly report to the help-desk manager of all codes, sorted by uses allowed and expiry, so long-lived codes get revoked.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting
• No Duo events and HTTP 401 in the input log under `$SPLUNK_HOME/var/log/splunk/duo_splunkapp/`: wrong secret key, an API hostname from a different Duo account, or clock skew on the input host.
• HTTP 403: the Admin API application is missing **Grant read log**.
• HTTP 429: Duo rate-limits the log endpoints. Make sure the deprecated 3504 connector and the 7404 input are not both polling the same Admin API application.
• Duplicate rows after migration: the 3504 connector and the 7404 input are both enabled for the same log type.
grandmaExplanation: We keep a list of every one-time Duo bypass code our help desk hands out and flag any without a matching support request.
